definitions.explanation: Footwear worn to protect and comfort the feet. A general term for shoes of all types.

examples.japanese: {靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}いでください。
{新|あたら}しい{靴|くつ}を{買|か}いました。
この{靴|くつ}は{小|ちい}さいです。
この{靴|くつ}はとても{歩|ある}きやすくて、{毎日|まいにち}{仕事|しごと}に{履|は}いていきます。
examples.english: These shoes are very easy to walk in, so I wear them to work every day.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}は{靴|くつ}が{濡|ぬ}れるので、{長|なが}い{靴|くつ}を{履|は}きます。{足|あし}が{濡|ぬ}れないから{便利|べんり}です。
examples.english: On rainy days I wear boots because regular shoes get wet. It's convenient because my feet don't get wet.

notes:
{靴|くつ} is the general word for shoes and footwear.

COUNTER:
{足|そく} - {一|いっ}{足|そく} (one pair), {二|に}{足|そく} (two pairs)

VERBS:
- {靴|くつ}を{履|は}く: to put on shoes
- {靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}ぐ: to take off shoes

TYPES OF FOOTWEAR:
- スニーカー: sneakers
- {革靴|かわぐつ}: leather shoes
- ブーツ: boots
- サンダル: sandals
- スリッパ: slippers

RELATED WORDS:
- {靴下|くつした}: socks
- {靴紐|くつひも}: shoelaces
- {靴箱|くつばこ}: shoe cabinet

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, shoes are removed when entering homes, schools, temples, and many traditional establishments. The {玄関|げんかん} (entryway) is where shoes are left.
